verdictReason: Leans kill but I could not re-verify the two facts a kill needs: seller earnings (case file says most TPT sellers earn $0-$100/month) and any existing migration tool. Verified: sellers own their IP and keep their own files, TPT can close accounts and withhold payouts, Payhip pages show single-file upload with no import link. No structural edge: any dev or Payhip could copy it; sale is one-off, no discovery off TPT. Assumption-only model is negative when pessimistic.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Manual relisting is the free status quo: Payhip's signup is free and its digital-download flow is single-file upload; the pages I read show no import or bulk-migration link (absence on a few pages, not proof that none exists). Destination alternatives are Payhip (case file: 5% per sale, not re-verified), Gumroad (10% + $0.50 on direct sales, 30% on marketplace-discovered sales) and a Stripe-direct store (2.9% + 30c per card transaction). Sellers also already hold their own source files, so the 'takes TPT product files' step is largely unnecessary; the real labour is re-creating titles, descriptions, covers and bundles. I could not search for existing paid migration tools because the search budget was exhausted.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None identified. The scan-1 edge is Payhip's 5% fee against TPT's take, which belongs to Payhip and not the entrant (the case file concedes this). A listing-migration utility has no exclusive data, licence or compounding asset: Payhip, Gumroad, a Shopify-style importer, a freelancer or a seller-community member could copy it quickly. Falsifier: a measured paid conversion from TPT sellers above about 2% at $19 with repeat/referral purchases, or evidence that no platform offers any import and sellers are asking for one.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Nobody demonstrated. The pain is real: TPT's terms allow closing any account 'at any time for any reason, with or without notice' and withholding payouts at its discretion (the case file adds a Trustpilot seller reporting $300 withheld, not re-read), and the marketplace is large (7M+ educators). But I found no listing, price or sale of a paid migration tool, and the case file's income data (most sellers earn $0-$100/month, E5) was not re-verified. The buyer is a low-revenue seller facing a one-off task, which caps price and repeat revenue.

answers.question: (4) Legal/platform constraints?
answers.answer: TPT's terms (updated 2025-12-08) say sellers own and maintain the intellectual property in their Resources, and I found no exclusivity clause in the text I read, so a seller relisting their own work is not barred by what I read. TPT may suspend accounts and withhold payouts at its discretion, which is the pain but also means a seller using an outside tool could lose their TPT account if TPT objects (unverified). I did not find a clause on automated access in the text I read (the page was truncated and not fully checked); a tool should work from files the seller supplies, never scrape TPT. Third-party clipart/font licences inside covers, buyer-licensed resources, Payhip's terms and API limits (no API read) are unverified.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers
answers.answer: Reference entrant, all assumptions: price $19 one-time per shop migration; 60 paid migrations in year 1 (first revenue about day 60, then about 6 per month); revenue $1,140. Cost $391: domain/hosting $60, support email/tools $60, acquisition test $100, per-sale cost $2.85 (card fees 2.9% + 30c on $19 is $0.85, AI/API $2.00). Base profit about $749 for about 470 hours (9 h/week), under $2/hour. Pessimistic (price x0.8 = $15.20, volume x0.5 = 30, cost x1.5): revenue $456, cost $587, profit -$131. Volume has no source; reaching sellers with no audience is the unresolved cost.

killReasons.reason: Buyer cannot pay much: case-file evidence says most TPT sellers earn $0-$100/month, so a one-off migration tool is a rounding error for the median seller and has no recurring revenue (E5 not re-verified, so held at major, not fatal).

Sellers own their IP and keep their source files (so the 'take TPT product files' step adds little) and Payhip's flow is a plain file upload; the paid value reduces to a one-time listing-copy and bundle task that a rival, Payhip or a freelancer could copy, with no exclusive asset.

Pain is real but it is the platform risk, not relisting labour: TPT can close accounts and withhold payouts at its discretion, yet leaving TPT also means losing its marketplace traffic (7M+ educators), so the migration tool does not solve discovery.
Platform dependency: any workflow touching a seller's TPT or Payhip account may break either platform's terms; no Payhip API or terms were read.

assumptions: ASSUMPTION: price $19 one-time per shop migration (no price in case file); chosen against sellers earning $0-$100/month
ASSUMPTION: 60 paid migrations in year 1, first revenue about day 60, then about 6 per month; no source for volume or conversion
ASSUMPTION: fixed cost $220 = domain/hosting $60 + support email/tools $60 + acquisition test $100
ASSUMPTION: per-sale cost $2.85 = card fees 2.9% + 30c on $19 (about $0.85, rate from Stripe's page) + AI/API $2.00
Cost exceeds the $350 reference cash by $41 and would be funded from revenue; owner time (about 470 hours at 9 h/week) is not costed
Pessimistic: price x0.8 = $15.20, volume x0.5 = 30 sales, cost x1.5 = $586.50 gives revenue $456 and profit -$130.50
Case-file 85% margin and 2-vs-10 hours relisting claims were not used: no price and no time source

legalNotes: TPT terms (2025-12-08): sellers own their resources' IP; I found no exclusivity clause in the text read, but the page was long and partly summarised, so a full read of terms is still needed (EDU-03-D1).
TPT may close accounts and withhold payouts at its discretion; a seller using an outside tool could be exposed if TPT objects (EDU-03-D2, EDU-03-D3).

Not verified: automated-access/scraping clauses in TPT terms, Payhip terms and API capabilities, third-party licences for clipart, fonts and covers, and buyer-licensed resources that sellers must not relist.
Design implication if pursued: only handle files the seller uploads and certifies as their own; do not scrape TPT.
unverified: TPT seller earnings distribution (seolumina page fetch was blocked; E5 is case-file evidence only)
Payhip fee level and plan structure (payhip.com/pricing could not be fetched; 5% figure is from the case file via learningmole, not re-read)
Whether any paid or free TPT-to-Payhip/Etsy migration tool already exists: WebSearch budget was exhausted before any search for it
Existence of Payhip product-creation API or import feature (help center and API pages could not be fetched)
Willingness to pay of TPT sellers, and any channel/CAC for reaching them without an audience
Trustpilot withheld-earnings report (E3), Quickshops pricing and relisting-time estimates: not re-read
TPT terms: only about 100k of 125k characters were summarised and automated-access language was not found, which is not proof it is absent
